:::{#cor-rank-product-full-rank}
#### Multiplying by a matrix of full rank does not change the rank

Let $\matr{A}$ be $m \times n$ and $\matr{B}$ be $n \times k$.

1. If $\matr{A}$ has full column rank (@def-full-column-rank), then $\operatorname{rank}(\matr{A} \matr{B}) = \operatorname{rank}(\matr{B})$.
2. If $\operatorname{rank}(\matr{B}) = n$, then $\operatorname{rank}(\matr{A} \matr{B}) = \operatorname{rank}(\matr{A})$.

:::

::: proof

**Part 1.**
Because $\matr{A}$ has [full column rank](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-full-column-rank), $\matr{A} \vecf{y} = \vzero_m$ only for $\vecf{y} = \vzero_n$
(@thm-independent-null-space).
So for $\vecf{x} \in \reals^k$,

$$
\ba
\matr{A} \matr{B} \vecf{x} = \vzero_m
&\iff \matr{B} \vecf{x} = \vzero_n
&& \text{(@thm-independent-null-space, with } \vecf{y} = \matr{B} \vecf{x} \text{)}
\ea
$$

so $\mathcal{N}(\matr{A} \matr{B}) = \mathcal{N}(\matr{B})$ (@def-null-space),
and the two matrices have the same nullity (@def-nullity).
Both have $k$ columns, so by @thm-rank-nullity they have the same [rank](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-rank).

**Part 2.**
$\mathcal{C}(\matr{B})$ is a [subspace](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-subspace) of $\reals^n$ (@thm-column-space-span) of [dimension](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-dimension) $n$ (@thm-rank-dim),
so $\mathcal{C}(\matr{B}) = \reals^n$ (@thm-subspace-equal-dim).
Every vector of $\mathcal{C}(\matr{A} \matr{B})$ is $\matr{A}\,(\matr{B} \vecf{x})$ for some $\vecf{x}$ (@def-column-space),
and $\matr{B} \vecf{x}$ takes every vector of $\reals^n$,
so $\mathcal{C}(\matr{A} \matr{B}) = \mathcal{C}(\matr{A})$ and the two matrices have the same rank (@thm-rank-dim).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-rank-product-full-rank}
#### Ranks of products with a full-rank factor

Let $\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$, which has [rank](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-rank) $1$.

- Part 1: $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ has two [linearly independent](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-linearly-independent) columns, so it has [full column rank](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-full-column-rank), and
  $\matr{A} \matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ has rank $1 = \operatorname{rank}(\matr{B})$.
- Part 2: let $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$, which has rank $1$, and let
  $\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$, which has rank $2$.
  Then $\matr{A} \matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ has rank $1 = \operatorname{rank}(\matr{A})$.

:::
